newsitem.title: USA: Chicago school pushing Puerto Rico independence.
newsitem.headline: Chicago school pushing Puerto Rico independence.

text.p: A public high school in Chicago has used government education funds to promote Puerto Rican independence and freedom for jailed backers of that cause, the Chicago Sun-Times reported Tuesday.

Quoting an internal school board report and other sources, the newspaper said the American flag was banned in some classrooms at Roberto Clemente High School and one speaker, brought to the school from Puerto Rico at taxpayers' expense, spat on a U.S. flag during his presentation.

Paul Vallas, chief executive officer for Chicago public schools, said the alleged financial irregularities have been under investigation since the school was put on financial probation 18 months ago. He told Reuters he was appointing a new principal for the school and a management team "that will be in place tomorrow."

The newspaper quoted one former student as saying he had seen one group "rake in as much as $10,000 a night from door proceeds at an event that was completely funded with money that should have gone to buy books for Clemente students."

It said the group involved has been working to free Puerto Ricans jailed for pro-independence activities including bombings and armed attacks dating back to 1974 blamed on the now-dormant FALN (Fuerzas Armadas de Liberacion Nacional).

The school, in a heavily Hispanic nieghborhood just west of downtown Chicago, has 2,500 students, nearly three-quarters of whom qualify for benefits under a state programme intended to educate the poor, the newspaper said. These poverty funds were used for some of the pro-independence programmes, it said.

The internal report cited by the newspaper said "the political climate and divisiveness (at the school) thwart academic progress at a level so significant that the eduction of the students is being ignored."

Vallas confirmed published reports that a woman who had been in line to become principal of Clemente turned down the job after she received threats alleged to have been from the FALN. But he said the situation was a result of internal politics among factions at the school and that invoking the FALN's name was probably an empty gesture on someone's part.
